verdict.rationale: A documented crawling and licensing stance is a fair question for a web search and retrieval API, so the axis applies. However, nothing in the evidence pack shows Exa publishing a policy on robots.txt compliance, content licensing, or permitted downstream use of results. The docs cover search types, contents extraction, pricing and MCP. A community post alleges Exa ignores robots.txt, but with no vendor claim to contradict, that cannot make this a dispute; it only confirms the absence of a documented stance.
